title: Gulf County School Board, District 1
what_it_does: School board members set the district budget and school-tax rate, hire the superintendent (where appointed), approve school boundaries, curriculum policy and construction, and set district policies. Nonpartisan.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); both candidates are marked Qualified, which for a nonpartisan seat means the August vote did not produce a majority winner (or the seat is decided only in November). Positions have not been researched; check the county Supervisor of Elections sample ballot.

candidates.name: Chad Bailey
candidates.occupation: Outside plant engineer, Consolidated Communications (Fidium); Gulf County School Board member, District 1
candidates.background: Chad Bailey works as an outside plant engineer for Consolidated Communications and was appointed to the Gulf County School Board's District 1 seat by Gov. Ron DeSantis in October 2025, filling the vacancy left by Denny McGlon. He is a children's minister and has been involved with local baseball programs and the high school bass fishing club. He led the August 2026 primary with about 46% and faces a November runoff.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

teacher_pay.summary: Bailey names teacher pay as a priority, saying neighboring counties can offer more and that the district is already working to improve salaries.
teacher_pay.quote: Some of our counties can offer better pay. As a sitting school board member, our district is currently working to improve our teachers' salaries.

sources.title: Three candidates are seeking the Gulf County School Board District 1 seat

education_choice.summary: Asked about school choice, Bailey did not take a position for or against public money following students, saying instead that the district's job is to make its own schools the place families want to be.
education_choice.quote: Our responsibility as a school district is to make our public schools a place where families want to be.

sources.title: Three candidates are seeking the Gulf County School Board District 1 seat

candidates.name: Dennis Peak
candidates.occupation: Owner, Peak's Ink screen printing; partner, Lighthouse Monument and Vault LLC
candidates.background: Dennis Peak is a Gulf County native and 1983 graduate of Port St. Joe High School. He owns a screen-printing business, is a partner in a monument company, also works at a local flooring store, and served about 20 years as the school district's booster club president.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

school_books.summary: Peak says much of what is being removed from schools is unnecessary and that the material is history, indicating he would not pull books over objections.
school_books.quote: I believe a lot of the things they are banishing out of the schools is not necessary. I think that's history.

sources.title: Three candidates are seeking the Gulf County School Board District 1 seat

education_choice.summary: Peak said school choice is an area he is not certain about and that he would want to research why families are choosing homeschooling before taking a position.
education_choice.quote: This is an area I'm not really sure of

sources.title: Three candidates are seeking the Gulf County School Board District 1 seat

other_issues.title: Local hiring and classroom behavior
other_issues.summary: Peak's stated first-year goal is bringing on more local teachers and administrators, arguing local staff are important influences on young people. He also raises classroom disruption as a concern and points to parental involvement as the remedy.

sources.title: Three candidates are seeking the Gulf County School Board District 1 seat
